_note:
THE DROWNED SHORE, the voices that are not scenes.

THE SIGNALMAN IS HOW TARIN IS FELT. Canon gives him the other half of the operation -- he is taking Meridian's towers off the ring while the player walks in at the front -- and the whole problem of writing that is that he is eleven miles of nothing away and can never be on screen. So there is a man on this beach with a glass on the north tower, and his line changes three times, on op_tower_1, op_tower_2 and op_tower_3, which are set by the three step beats up on the platform in data/events/eastreach_platform.json.

The player therefore hears about Tarin's work TWICE and from two directions: the deck lurching under their own feet as each relay goes, and then, if they walk back down for a heal, a man on a beach telling them the count. Neither of those is Tarin saying anything, and that is the point of the whole arrangement.

TALLOW READS THE WATER because that is her entire character -- she reads piles for a living and Mirehaven is agreed rather than built -- and she is the only person in the act who says out loud that the sea is behaving like something is under it.

lines: Three. All three, and the fourth went before I had the glass back up.
Whatever else happens on this island today, that boy did his part of it.
Two. Two towers dark, and the second one came a quarter of an hour early.
He is going faster than he told anybody he would, which is very like him.
One. The north tower has gone out and it has stayed out.
He said he would do them in order and he has started in order.
I have a glass on the north tower and nothing on it yet.
Three flashes when a relay goes. That was his idea and I told him it was showing off.
The set of it changed when that tower went dark. Within the minute.
I have read piles for thirty years. Water does not answer machinery. It is answering something else.
This shingle is a week old. Two, at the outside.
The sea threw all of this up here recently and in a hurry, and I would like to know what for.
One of the anchor towers has stopped. I felt the legs take it up through the shingle.
That is nineteen people and a boy from Hearthmere doing something I could not have planned.
Every doorway down there faces the same way. Inland, away from the sea.
They knew. Three thousand years ago they built this town knowing which way to face.
